1	import { Meta, Unstyled } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
2	import { DocFooter } from '../../../storybook/blocks/doc-page';
3	import { DocLink } from '../../../storybook/blocks/doc-link';
4	import {
5	  Anatomy,
6	  ComponentHeader,
7	  ComponentPage,
8	  Do,
9	  Dont,
10	  Example,
11	  Guidelines,
12	  Key,
13	  Keyboard,
14	  Part,
15	  PropsTable,
16	  Related,
17	  Section,
18	  Subsection,
19	  TokensTable,
20	  Usage,
21	  UseFor,
22	  UseInstead,
23	} from '../../../storybook/blocks/component-page';
24	import { Button } from '../../atoms/button';
25	import { Field } from '../../molecules/field';
26	import { TextArea } from '../../molecules/text-area';
27	import { TextField } from '../../molecules/text-field';
28	import { DatePicker } from '../date-picker';
29	import { Form, FormFooter, FormRow, FormSection } from './form';
30	import formStyles from './form.module.css';
31	import * as FormStories from './Form.stories';
32	
33	export const stop = (event) => event.preventDefault();
34	
35	{/* Multi-line code samples. Written as exports, because MDX strips two spaces of indent from every line of a multi-line string in a JSX attribute. */}
36	
37	export const sample1 = `<FormFooter>
38	  <Button prominence="tertiary" onClick={onCancel}>Cancel</Button>
39	  <Button prominence="primary" type="submit">Create matter</Button>
40	</FormFooter>`;
41	export const sample2 = `<FormFooter>
42	  <Button prominence="primary">Create matter</Button>
43	</FormFooter>`;
44	export const sample3 = `<FormRow>
45	  <Field label="City"><TextField /></Field>
46	  <Field label="State"><TextField /></Field>
47	  <Field label="ZIP"><TextField inputMode="numeric" /></Field>
48	</FormRow>`;
49	export const sample4 = `<FormRow>
50	  <Field label="Notes"><TextArea /></Field>
51	  <Field label="Email"><TextField type="email" /></Field>
52	</FormRow>`;
53	export const sample5 = `<Form title="New matter" requiredLegend>
54	  <FormSection>
55	    <Field label="Matter name" required><TextField /></Field>
56	  </FormSection>
57	</Form>`;
58	export const sample6 = `<Form title="New matter">
59	  <FormSection>
60	    <Field label="Matter name" required><TextField /></Field>
61	  </FormSection>
62	</Form>`;
63	
64	<Meta of={FormStories} name="Docs" />
65	
66	<Unstyled>
67	<ComponentPage>
68	
69	<ComponentHeader
70	  id="form"
71	  example={
72	    <Form title="New matter" description="Open a matter for an existing client." requiredLegend onSubmit={stop}>
73	      <FormSection title="Client">
74	        <FormRow>
75	          <Field label="First name" required>
76	            <TextField defaultValue="Jordan" />
77	          </Field>
78	          <Field label="Last name" required>
79	            <TextField defaultValue="Lee" />
80	          </Field>
81	        </FormRow>
82	        <Field label="Email" message="We'll send the engagement letter here.">
83	          <TextField type="email" defaultValue="jordan.lee@example.com" />
84	        </Field>
85	      </FormSection>
86	      <FormSection title="Matter">
87	        <FormRow>
88	          <Field label="Matter name" required>
89	            <TextField defaultValue="Lee Living Trust" />
90	          </Field>
91	          <Field label="Opened">
92	            <DatePicker defaultValue={new Date(2026, 2, 9)} today={new Date(2026, 2, 9)} />
93	          </Field>
94	        </FormRow>
95	      </FormSection>
96	      <FormFooter>
97	        <Button prominence="tertiary">Cancel</Button>
98	        <Button prominence="primary" type="submit">Create matter</Button>
99	      </FormFooter>
100	    </Form>
101	  }
102	>
103	  Form lays out a set of fields someone fills in and submits together: a header, sections of fields,
104	  rows that put fields side by side, and a footer for the actions. It renders a native `form` and
105	  leaves the fields, their state, and submitting to you.
106	</ComponentHeader>
107	
108	<Section title="When to use">
109	
110	<Usage>
111	<UseFor>
112	
113	- Any set of fields submitted together: a new matter, a client's details, settings.
114	- Grouping a long form into titled sections.
115	- Putting short, related fields on one line, such as first and last name.
116	
117	</UseFor>
118	<UseInstead>
119	
120	- **One control on its own, such as a search box:** <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Field" />, or the control with its own label.
121	- **A value edited in place, outside a form:** <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Inline Edit" />.
122	- **A short form in a dialog:** <DocLink to="Components/Overlays/Modal Dialog" />, with the fields inside it.
123	
124	</UseInstead>
125	</Usage>
126	
127	</Section>
128	
129	<Section title="Anatomy">
130	
131	<Anatomy
132	  specimen={
133	    <Form title="New matter" description="Open a matter for an existing client." requiredLegend onSubmit={stop}>
134	      <FormSection title="Client">
135	        <FormRow>
136	          <Field label="First name" required>
137	            <TextField defaultValue="Jordan" />
138	          </Field>
139	          <Field label="Last name" required>
140	            <TextField defaultValue="Lee" />
141	          </Field>
142	        </FormRow>
143	      </FormSection>
144	      <FormFooter>
145	        <Button prominence="tertiary">Cancel</Button>
146	        <Button prominence="primary" type="submit">Create matter</Button>
147	      </FormFooter>
148	    </Form>
149	  }
150	>
151	  <Part name="root" target={formStyles.root}>The native `form`, as wide as its container. It takes any other attribute you pass, such as `onSubmit` and `noValidate`.</Part>
152	  <Part name="header" target={formStyles.header}>Shown when `title`, `description`, or `requiredLegend` is set.</Part>
153	  <Part name="title" target={formStyles.title}>`title`, as text in a `div`, not a heading.</Part>
154	  <Part name="description" target={formStyles.description}>`description`, as a paragraph. The required legend is a second paragraph with the same style.</Part>
155	  <Part name="requiredMark" target={formStyles.requiredMark}>The legend's `*`, in the error color, the same mark Field shows on a required field.</Part>
156	  <Part name="section" target={formStyles.section}>A FormSection: a group of fields with an optional title, spaced from what's above it.</Part>
157	  <Part name="row" target={formStyles.row}>A FormRow: its fields side by side, in equal columns.</Part>
158	  <Part name="footer" target={formStyles.footer}>A FormFooter: the actions, at the end of the line by default.</Part>
159	</Anatomy>
160	
161	</Section>
162	
163	<Section title="Behavior">
164	
165	<Subsection title="Header">
166	
167	`title` and `description` make the header, and `requiredLegend` adds the line "\* indicates a
168	required field", with the `*` in the error color to match Field's required mark. Set it when any
169	field is required. Without all three, there's no header. The text after the `*` is
170	`requiredLegendLabel`; pass a translation.
171	
172	<Example of={FormStories.Playground} />
173	
174	</Subsection>
175	
176	<Subsection title="Sections">
177	
178	A FormSection groups related fields and puts space above them, so it separates them from the header
179	or the section before. Its `title` is optional. Put Fields straight in a section to stack them one per
180	line, at the full width.
181	
182	<Example of={FormStories.Sections} />
183	
184	</Subsection>
185	
186	<Subsection title="Rows">
187	
188	A FormRow puts its fields side by side in equal columns. Figma designs rows of up to four. A row
189	stays on one line at every width: it doesn't stack on a narrow screen, so keep rows to short fields
190	that fit.
191	
192	<Example of={FormStories.Rows} />
193	
194	</Subsection>
195	
196	<Subsection title="Footer">
197	
198	A FormFooter holds the actions, with more space above it than between sections. `align="end"`, the
199	default, puts them at the end of the line; `align="start"` puts them at the start. It spaces its
200	Buttons the way Button Group does, so put the Buttons straight in it.
201	
202	<Example of={FormStories.FooterAlignment} />
203	
204	</Subsection>
205	
206	<Subsection title="Submitting">
207	
208	Form keeps no state of its own. It's a native `form`, so `onSubmit` fires when someone presses a
209	`type="submit"` Button, or Enter in a single-line field, and the browser checks `required` and other
210	constraints first unless you set `noValidate`. Each field's value, error, and message are yours,
211	through Field.
212	
213	<Example of={FormStories.EdgeCases} caption="Edge cases: a form with no header, and a form on a dark surface." />
214	
215	</Subsection>
216	
217	<Subsection title="Disabling a group of fields">
218	
219	To disable several fields at once, put them in a native `fieldset` with `disabled`. Every form
220	control in the system follows it as it follows its own `disabled`: it looks disabled, leaves the tab
221	order, and can't be changed or opened. A FormSection is a `div`, so put the `fieldset` inside it,
222	and clear the browser's own border, padding, and margin. Field's label doesn't dim, with a fieldset
223	or the control's own `disabled`.
224	
225	<Example of={FormStories.DisabledFieldset} caption="A closed matter's details, locked by a disabled fieldset until the matter is reopened." />
226	
227	</Subsection>
228	
229	<Subsection title="When errors show">
230	
231	Form doesn't check anything itself, but when its errors show follows one rule across the system:
232	
233	1. **Check when the form is submitted**, not while someone is still typing.
234	2. **Show every error at once**: a Section Message with `tone="error"` at the top of the form,
235	   whose `errors` name each field that needs fixing and link to it, and each field's own error
236	   through Field. Move focus to the summary.
237	3. **Then update each field's error as its value changes**, so it clears as soon as it's fixed. The
238	   summary is a live region, so it changes only on the next submit.
239	
240	Set `noValidate` when you show the system's errors, so the browser's own messages don't come first.
241	<DocLink to="Patterns/Forms and Validation" /> builds the whole flow.
242	
243	</Subsection>
244	
245	</Section>
246	
247	<Section title="Do and don't">
248	
249	<Guidelines>
250	<Do
251	  caption="Give the submitting Button type submit, so it submits the form."
252	  code={sample1}
253	>
254	  <Form onSubmit={stop}>
255	    <FormFooter>
256	      <Button prominence="tertiary">Cancel</Button>
257	      <Button prominence="primary" type="submit">Create matter</Button>
258	    </FormFooter>
259	  </Form>
260	</Do>
261	<Dont
262	  caption="Leave the submitting Button's type unset. Button defaults to type button, so it doesn't submit."
263	  code={sample2}
264	/>
265	<Do
266	  caption="Put short, related fields in a row, such as city, state, and ZIP."
267	  code={sample3}
268	>
269	  <Form onSubmit={stop}>
270	    <FormRow>
271	      <Field label="City">
272	        <TextField defaultValue="Trenton" />
273	      </Field>
274	      <Field label="State">
275	        <TextField defaultValue="NJ" />
276	      </Field>
277	      <Field label="ZIP">
278	        <TextField inputMode="numeric" defaultValue="08608" />
279	      </Field>
280	    </FormRow>
281	  </Form>
282	</Do>
283	<Dont
284	  caption="Put a long field beside an unrelated one to save space. The row never stacks, so both get cramped."
285	  code={sample4}
286	>
287	  <Form onSubmit={stop}>
288	    <FormRow>
289	      <Field label="Notes">
290	        <TextArea defaultValue="Client prefers a call before any filing." />
291	      </Field>
292	      <Field label="Email">
293	        <TextField type="email" defaultValue="jordan.lee@example.com" />
294	      </Field>
295	    </FormRow>
296	  </Form>
297	</Dont>
298	<Do
299	  caption="Set requiredLegend when the form marks required fields, so the * is explained."
300	  code={sample5}
301	>
302	  <Form title="New matter" requiredLegend onSubmit={stop}>
303	    <FormSection>
304	      <Field label="Matter name" required>
305	        <TextField />
306	      </Field>
307	    </FormSection>
308	  </Form>
309	</Do>
310	<Dont
311	  caption="Mark fields required with no legend. Not everyone knows what the * means."
312	  code={sample6}
313	>
314	  <Form title="New matter" onSubmit={stop}>
315	    <FormSection>
316	      <Field label="Matter name" required>
317	        <TextField />
318	      </Field>
319	    </FormSection>
320	  </Form>
321	</Dont>
322	</Guidelines>
323	
324	</Section>
325	
326	<Section title="Accessibility">
327	
328	- Form renders a native `form`, so submitting with Enter or a submit button, and the browser's own
329	  checks, work with no extra code.
330	- A form is announced as a form landmark only when it has a name, and `title` doesn't give it one.
331	  Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` if people should find the form by landmark.
332	- The title and the section titles are text in a `div`, not headings, so they aren't in the page's
333	  heading outline. Put the page's own heading above the form when it needs one. A FormSection is a
334	  `div`, not a `fieldset`, so its title isn't announced with the fields in it.
335	- The required legend is read as text, `*` included. Field hides its own `*` from assistive
336	  technology and sets the control's native `required` instead.
337	- Each field's name, description, and error come from Field. Form doesn't change them.
338	- Errors show on submit, all at once, so nobody is interrupted while typing. Form doesn't move focus
339	  when a submit fails: move it to the summary at the top, whose `errors` links move focus to each
340	  field.
341	
342	Form adds no keys of its own; the browser handles moving through fields and submitting.
343	
344	<Keyboard>
345	  <Key keys="Tab">Moves through the fields and the footer's buttons, in the order they're written.</Key>
346	  <Key keys="Enter">In a single-line field, submits the form, as the browser does when the form has a submit button.</Key>
347	</Keyboard>
348	
349	</Section>
350	
351	<Section title="API">
352	
353	<PropsTable of={FormStories} native="form" />
354	
355	<Subsection title="FormSection">
356	
357	<PropsTable component={FormSection} native="div" />
358	
359	</Subsection>
360	
361	<Subsection title="FormRow">
362	
363	<PropsTable component={FormRow} native="div" />
364	
365	</Subsection>
366	
367	<Subsection title="FormFooter">
368	
369	<PropsTable component={FormFooter} native="div" />
370	
371	</Subsection>
372	
373	</Section>
374	
375	<Section title="Design tokens">
376	
377	Every token Form's stylesheet uses, by family, with the property it sets and when. "Base" is the form
378	element; the header, title, description, sections, rows, and footer are its parts. All the space
379	between parts sits on the parts themselves, so a form without a header doesn't start with a gap.
380	
381	<TokensTable id="form" />
382	
383	</Section>
384	
385	<Section title="Related components">
386	
387	<Related>
388	
389	- <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Field" />, which gives each control its label, message, and required mark.
390	- <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Text Field" />, <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Text Area" />, and <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Select" />, the controls most forms hold.
391	- <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Date Picker" /> and <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Time Picker" /> for dates and times.
392	- <DocLink to="Components/Actions/Button" /> for the footer's actions.
393	- <DocLink to="Components/Overlays/Modal Dialog" /> for a short form in a dialog.
394	
395	</Related>
396	
397	</Section>
398	
399	<DocFooter>
400	  The API tables read form.types.ts, the design tokens read form.module.css, and the Figma source
401	  comes from registry.json, so they follow the code.
402	</DocFooter>
403	
404	</ComponentPage>
405	</Unstyled>
406

import { Meta, Unstyled } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import { DocFooter } from '../../../storybook/blocks/doc-page';
import { DocLink } from '../../../storybook/blocks/doc-link';
import {
  Anatomy,
  ComponentHeader,
  ComponentPage,
  Do,
  Dont,
  Example,
  Guidelines,
  Key,
  Keyboard,
  Part,
  PropsTable,
  Related,
  Section,
  Subsection,
  TokensTable,
  Usage,
  UseFor,
  UseInstead,
} from '../../../storybook/blocks/component-page';
import { Button } from '../../atoms/button';
import { Field } from '../../molecules/field';
import { TextArea } from '../../molecules/text-area';
import { TextField } from '../../molecules/text-field';
import { DatePicker } from '../date-picker';
import { Form, FormFooter, FormRow, FormSection } from './form';
import formStyles from './form.module.css';
import * as FormStories from './Form.stories';

export const stop = (event) => event.preventDefault();

{/* Multi-line code samples. Written as exports, because MDX strips two spaces of indent from every line of a multi-line string in a JSX attribute. */}

export const sample1 = `<FormFooter>
  <Button prominence="tertiary" onClick={onCancel}>Cancel</Button>
  <Button prominence="primary" type="submit">Create matter</Button>
</FormFooter>`;
export const sample2 = `<FormFooter>
  <Button prominence="primary">Create matter</Button>
</FormFooter>`;
export const sample3 = `<FormRow>
  <Field label="City"><TextField /></Field>
  <Field label="State"><TextField /></Field>
  <Field label="ZIP"><TextField inputMode="numeric" /></Field>
</FormRow>`;
export const sample4 = `<FormRow>
  <Field label="Notes"><TextArea /></Field>
  <Field label="Email"><TextField type="email" /></Field>
</FormRow>`;
export const sample5 = `<Form title="New matter" requiredLegend>
  <FormSection>
    <Field label="Matter name" required><TextField /></Field>
  </FormSection>
</Form>`;
export const sample6 = `<Form title="New matter">
  <FormSection>
    <Field label="Matter name" required><TextField /></Field>
  </FormSection>
</Form>`;

<Meta of={FormStories} name="Docs" />

<Unstyled>
<ComponentPage>

<ComponentHeader
  id="form"
  example={
    <Form title="New matter" description="Open a matter for an existing client." requiredLegend onSubmit={stop}>
      <FormSection title="Client">
        <FormRow>
          <Field label="First name" required>
            <TextField defaultValue="Jordan" />
          </Field>
          <Field label="Last name" required>
            <TextField defaultValue="Lee" />
          </Field>
        </FormRow>
        <Field label="Email" message="We'll send the engagement letter here.">
          <TextField type="email" defaultValue="jordan.lee@example.com" />
        </Field>
      </FormSection>
      <FormSection title="Matter">
        <FormRow>
          <Field label="Matter name" required>
            <TextField defaultValue="Lee Living Trust" />
          </Field>
          <Field label="Opened">
            <DatePicker defaultValue={new Date(2026, 2, 9)} today={new Date(2026, 2, 9)} />
          </Field>
        </FormRow>
      </FormSection>
      <FormFooter>
        <Button prominence="tertiary">Cancel</Button>
        <Button prominence="primary" type="submit">Create matter</Button>
      </FormFooter>
    </Form>
  }
>
  Form lays out a set of fields someone fills in and submits together: a header, sections of fields,
  rows that put fields side by side, and a footer for the actions. It renders a native `form` and
  leaves the fields, their state, and submitting to you.
</ComponentHeader>

<Section title="When to use">

<Usage>
<UseFor>

- Any set of fields submitted together: a new matter, a client's details, settings.
- Grouping a long form into titled sections.
- Putting short, related fields on one line, such as first and last name.

</UseFor>
<UseInstead>

- **One control on its own, such as a search box:** <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Field" />, or the control with its own label.
- **A value edited in place, outside a form:** <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Inline Edit" />.
- **A short form in a dialog:** <DocLink to="Components/Overlays/Modal Dialog" />, with the fields inside it.

</UseInstead>
</Usage>

</Section>

<Section title="Anatomy">

<Anatomy
  specimen={
    <Form title="New matter" description="Open a matter for an existing client." requiredLegend onSubmit={stop}>
      <FormSection title="Client">
        <FormRow>
          <Field label="First name" required>
            <TextField defaultValue="Jordan" />
          </Field>
          <Field label="Last name" required>
            <TextField defaultValue="Lee" />
          </Field>
        </FormRow>
      </FormSection>
      <FormFooter>
        <Button prominence="tertiary">Cancel</Button>
        <Button prominence="primary" type="submit">Create matter</Button>
      </FormFooter>
    </Form>
  }
>
  <Part name="root" target={formStyles.root}>The native `form`, as wide as its container. It takes any other attribute you pass, such as `onSubmit` and `noValidate`.</Part>
  <Part name="header" target={formStyles.header}>Shown when `title`, `description`, or `requiredLegend` is set.</Part>
  <Part name="title" target={formStyles.title}>`title`, as text in a `div`, not a heading.</Part>
  <Part name="description" target={formStyles.description}>`description`, as a paragraph. The required legend is a second paragraph with the same style.</Part>
  <Part name="requiredMark" target={formStyles.requiredMark}>The legend's `*`, in the error color, the same mark Field shows on a required field.</Part>
  <Part name="section" target={formStyles.section}>A FormSection: a group of fields with an optional title, spaced from what's above it.</Part>
  <Part name="row" target={formStyles.row}>A FormRow: its fields side by side, in equal columns.</Part>
  <Part name="footer" target={formStyles.footer}>A FormFooter: the actions, at the end of the line by default.</Part>
</Anatomy>

</Section>

<Section title="Behavior">

<Subsection title="Header">

`title` and `description` make the header, and `requiredLegend` adds the line "\* indicates a
required field", with the `*` in the error color to match Field's required mark. Set it when any
field is required. Without all three, there's no header. The text after the `*` is
`requiredLegendLabel`; pass a translation.

<Example of={FormStories.Playground} />

</Subsection>

<Subsection title="Sections">

A FormSection groups related fields and puts space above them, so it separates them from the header
or the section before. Its `title` is optional. Put Fields straight in a section to stack them one per
line, at the full width.

<Example of={FormStories.Sections} />

</Subsection>

<Subsection title="Rows">

A FormRow puts its fields side by side in equal columns. Figma designs rows of up to four. A row
stays on one line at every width: it doesn't stack on a narrow screen, so keep rows to short fields
that fit.

<Example of={FormStories.Rows} />

</Subsection>

<Subsection title="Footer">

A FormFooter holds the actions, with more space above it than between sections. `align="end"`, the
default, puts them at the end of the line; `align="start"` puts them at the start. It spaces its
Buttons the way Button Group does, so put the Buttons straight in it.

<Example of={FormStories.FooterAlignment} />

</Subsection>

<Subsection title="Submitting">

Form keeps no state of its own. It's a native `form`, so `onSubmit` fires when someone presses a
`type="submit"` Button, or Enter in a single-line field, and the browser checks `required` and other
constraints first unless you set `noValidate`. Each field's value, error, and message are yours,
through Field.

<Example of={FormStories.EdgeCases} caption="Edge cases: a form with no header, and a form on a dark surface." />

</Subsection>

<Subsection title="Disabling a group of fields">

To disable several fields at once, put them in a native `fieldset` with `disabled`. Every form
control in the system follows it as it follows its own `disabled`: it looks disabled, leaves the tab
order, and can't be changed or opened. A FormSection is a `div`, so put the `fieldset` inside it,
and clear the browser's own border, padding, and margin. Field's label doesn't dim, with a fieldset
or the control's own `disabled`.

<Example of={FormStories.DisabledFieldset} caption="A closed matter's details, locked by a disabled fieldset until the matter is reopened." />

</Subsection>

<Subsection title="When errors show">

Form doesn't check anything itself, but when its errors show follows one rule across the system:

1. **Check when the form is submitted**, not while someone is still typing.
2. **Show every error at once**: a Section Message with `tone="error"` at the top of the form,
   whose `errors` name each field that needs fixing and link to it, and each field's own error
   through Field. Move focus to the summary.
3. **Then update each field's error as its value changes**, so it clears as soon as it's fixed. The
   summary is a live region, so it changes only on the next submit.

Set `noValidate` when you show the system's errors, so the browser's own messages don't come first.
<DocLink to="Patterns/Forms and Validation" /> builds the whole flow.

</Subsection>

</Section>

<Section title="Do and don't">

<Guidelines>
<Do
  caption="Give the submitting Button type submit, so it submits the form."
  code={sample1}
>
  <Form onSubmit={stop}>
    <FormFooter>
      <Button prominence="tertiary">Cancel</Button>
      <Button prominence="primary" type="submit">Create matter</Button>
    </FormFooter>
  </Form>
</Do>
<Dont
  caption="Leave the submitting Button's type unset. Button defaults to type button, so it doesn't submit."
  code={sample2}
/>
<Do
  caption="Put short, related fields in a row, such as city, state, and ZIP."
  code={sample3}
>
  <Form onSubmit={stop}>
    <FormRow>
      <Field label="City">
        <TextField defaultValue="Trenton" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="State">
        <TextField defaultValue="NJ" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="ZIP">
        <TextField inputMode="numeric" defaultValue="08608" />
      </Field>
    </FormRow>
  </Form>
</Do>
<Dont
  caption="Put a long field beside an unrelated one to save space. The row never stacks, so both get cramped."
  code={sample4}
>
  <Form onSubmit={stop}>
    <FormRow>
      <Field label="Notes">
        <TextArea defaultValue="Client prefers a call before any filing." />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Email">
        <TextField type="email" defaultValue="jordan.lee@example.com" />
      </Field>
    </FormRow>
  </Form>
</Dont>
<Do
  caption="Set requiredLegend when the form marks required fields, so the * is explained."
  code={sample5}
>
  <Form title="New matter" requiredLegend onSubmit={stop}>
    <FormSection>
      <Field label="Matter name" required>
        <TextField />
      </Field>
    </FormSection>
  </Form>
</Do>
<Dont
  caption="Mark fields required with no legend. Not everyone knows what the * means."
  code={sample6}
>
  <Form title="New matter" onSubmit={stop}>
    <FormSection>
      <Field label="Matter name" required>
        <TextField />
      </Field>
    </FormSection>
  </Form>
</Dont>
</Guidelines>

</Section>

<Section title="Accessibility">

- Form renders a native `form`, so submitting with Enter or a submit button, and the browser's own
  checks, work with no extra code.
- A form is announced as a form landmark only when it has a name, and `title` doesn't give it one.
  Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` if people should find the form by landmark.
- The title and the section titles are text in a `div`, not headings, so they aren't in the page's
  heading outline. Put the page's own heading above the form when it needs one. A FormSection is a
  `div`, not a `fieldset`, so its title isn't announced with the fields in it.
- The required legend is read as text, `*` included. Field hides its own `*` from assistive
  technology and sets the control's native `required` instead.
- Each field's name, description, and error come from Field. Form doesn't change them.
- Errors show on submit, all at once, so nobody is interrupted while typing. Form doesn't move focus
  when a submit fails: move it to the summary at the top, whose `errors` links move focus to each
  field.

Form adds no keys of its own; the browser handles moving through fields and submitting.

<Keyboard>
  <Key keys="Tab">Moves through the fields and the footer's buttons, in the order they're written.</Key>
  <Key keys="Enter">In a single-line field, submits the form, as the browser does when the form has a submit button.</Key>
</Keyboard>

</Section>

<Section title="API">

<PropsTable of={FormStories} native="form" />

<Subsection title="FormSection">

<PropsTable component={FormSection} native="div" />

</Subsection>

<Subsection title="FormRow">

</Subsection>

</Subsection>

</Section>

<Section title="Design tokens">

Every token Form's stylesheet uses, by family, with the property it sets and when. "Base" is the form
element; the header, title, description, sections, rows, and footer are its parts. All the space
between parts sits on the parts themselves, so a form without a header doesn't start with a gap.

<TokensTable id="form" />

</Section>

<Section title="Related components">

<Related>

- <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Field" />, which gives each control its label, message, and required mark.
- <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Text Field" />, <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Text Area" />, and <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Select" />, the controls most forms hold.
- <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Date Picker" /> and <DocLink to="Components/Forms/Time Picker" /> for dates and times.
- <DocLink to="Components/Actions/Button" /> for the footer's actions.
- <DocLink to="Components/Overlays/Modal Dialog" /> for a short form in a dialog.

</Related>

</Section>

</DocFooter>
